To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully introduced resistive interfilaments barriers in Bi(2223) tapes and that we have successfully developed a new ring bundle conductor concept with a central resistively coated strontium carbonate layer.
the resistive interfilaments barriers are a very promising alternative to reduce AC losses and that the new conductor geometry is an interesting concept for multifilament Bi(2223) tapes.
the novel resistive strontia-carbonate barriers are a very promising alternative approach to reduce the AC loss component coupling losses in multifilament BSCCO tapes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation, the characterization and the optimization of the superconducting Bi(2223) tapes and the development of a new tape geometry with a resistive core.
the development of new conductor geometries with a reduced coupling current loss.
the improvement of the AC loss performance of multifilamentary BSCCO tapes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resistive interfilamental barriers in the Bi-2212 matrix are not effective in reducing the coupling losses.
the resistive barriers are effective for the reduction of coupling losses.
the new conductor design has a very high potential for the application of high field superconducting magnets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resistive barriers are a powerful tool for reducing the coupling losses.
we have developed a new concept for Bi(2223) conductors which can be used for high field magnets with low AC losses.
the coupling losses could be reduced by a factor of 2.5 in the case of the ring bundles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resistive interfilaments are a very efficient method for reducing the coupling losses and can be applied in multifilament Bi(2223) tapes.
the coupling losses in the new conductor are reduced by a factor of 2 compared to a standard tape.
the resistive strontial carbonate barriers reduce the AC coupling losses significantly and the tapes show a very low AC loss density of 0.1 mWcm/sup -3/ at 4.2 K, 1 T, 10 Hz.
